Designing a Local-First Knowledge Base

By Ada Stone

A durable knowledge base starts with files you can read, move, and back up without asking a service for permission. Plain text remains useful because it does not depend on a particular application.

Keep the source

Every clipped article should preserve its original context. A title alone rarely tells you where an idea came from or how to find it again.

Tools come and go, but readable files remain.
  • Use descriptive filenames.
  • Keep metadata close to the content.
  • Make exports easy to test.

Local-first does not mean isolated. It means the local copy is always available, while synchronization and publishing remain deliberate choices made by the owner.
